A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 26-page paper, including Appendices A-L. Text, equations, tables, and rendered scientific content support reliable comparison; only the publication header and arXiv stamp differ.

before.justification: Section 4 and the experimental appendices report original synthetic and real-image bandit experiments, including attack success rates, timings, perturbation magnitudes, and defense results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Section 4 and the appendices, including the numerical results in Figures 1-11 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The full-trajectory, trajectory-free, and Online Score-Aware attacks, reward-model formulations, and shuffling defense are unchanged, including Algorithms 1-3 in Appendix K.

E1.justification: Both retain the same synthetic tasks and GenAI-Bench-based image evaluations, with identical generators, reward models, randomized-reward experiments, and bandit test scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator sets, including the attack variants, optimal-solution reference, and random-noise comparison in Sections 4.1, 4.2, and 4.6.

E3.justification: Metrics, configurations, and procedures are identical, including the 30-prompt evaluation, Table 1 settings, and Appendix E's 80/20 data split and 100-epoch training.

E4.justification: The dimensionality and network-width sweeps, constraint-count analysis, defense tests, random-noise tests, perturbation geometry, and real-data case study are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same image-generation seeds, ranging from 1 to 100. Repeated-run information, uncertainty displays, and statistical reporting practices are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All result entries and findings match across Figures 1-11, Table 1, and the accompanying text, including Figure 1's reported 100% attack success and Table 1's ETC and epsilon-greedy timings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4, Corollary 3.2, and Appendix B's lemmas, derivations, and proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reward-model attacks before training, high-dimensional vulnerability, efficient attack heuristics, and partial defense.

C2.justification: Both retain the same mechanism explanations, qualifications concerning OSA theory and incomplete defense, and practical threat-model interpretation in Appendix I.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training instructions, and pseudocode in Appendices D, E, and K are unchanged. The code-availability statement and repository link are also identical.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix A are identical, including the positioning relative to reward poisoning, context poisoning, and corruption-robust bandit research.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Accepted as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'. The arXiv stamp changes from v1, 2 February 2026, to v2, 3 June 2026. Body prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-11, Table 1, algorithm displays, captions, and their placement are unchanged. The publication-text updates do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v2 only updates the publication header and arXiv identification. The scientific content, supporting evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and appendix material are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
